title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Aisha Kumar
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood's core people policies and practical guidance for working at Redwood: role definitions and career ladders, compensation and benefits highlights, our hiring and onboarding process, and the set of internal tools and access flows new and existing employees need to be productive. It is intended for all Redwoods and managers; people-ops maintains ownership and updates quarterly or on policy change.

Quick links (internal): People-ops portal, IT access request form, Manager toolkit, Performance calibration guide, Role description library.

1) Roles & Career Ladders

Summary: We maintain standardized ladders for individual contributors (IC), engineering managers (EM), product managers (PM), research, and applied ML roles. Each ladder includes: expectations, competencies, sample deliverables, promotion criteria, and calibration guidance.

IC Engineering Ladder (summary):
- IC-1 (New grad / early career): Contributes to codebase with guidance, completes scoped tickets, writes tests.
- IC-2 (Engineer): Owns small features, participates in design reviews, debugs infra-level issues.
- IC-3 (Senior Engineer): Leads medium-sized features, mentors junior engineers, designs system components, owns SLIs for product areas.
- IC-4 (Staff Engineer): Cross-team impact, architectural leadership, leads postmortems and performance initiatives.
- IC-5 (Principal / Distinguished): Company-wide technical strategy, major platform initiatives, recognized external thought leadership (optional).

Manager Ladder (summary):
- EM-1 (Engineering Manager): Manages 1-6 engineers, responsible for delivery and growth plans.
- EM-2 (Senior Manager): Manages managers or larger teams, owns cross-team delivery.
- Director/VP: Strategic leadership and org planning.

Role definitions and examples: For each team there is a standard role-description document in the Role description library. Managers should review the appropriate role template before hiring or writing goals.

Promotion process (high level):
1. Nomination by manager (or self-nomination for IC-1->IC-2).
2. Evidence packet: summary of impact, examples of work, peer feedback, metrics.
3. Calibration & interview (if cross-role or skip-level required).
4. Promotion committee review (people-ops + hiring managers) and timeline: target 6-8 weeks from nomination.

2) Performance & Career Development

- Goal setting: Quarterly goals owned in the Performance tool. Goals should be outcome-focused and measurable.
- 1:1 cadence: Managers are expected to meet with direct reports weekly (30-60 min).
- Career conversations: At least once per quarter; document career plan and milestones.
- Learning budget: $1,500/year per employee (requests via people-ops).

3) Benefits & Perks (high-level summary)

Health & wellness:
- Medical: Multiple plan options (PPO and HMO) with employer premium contribution; full details on People-ops benefits page.
- Dental & vision: Company-sponsored PPO options.
- Wellness stipend: $100/month (reimbursable for gym, classes, therapy apps, or ergonomic equipment).

Financial benefits:
- 401(k): Company match up to 4% of salary.
- Equity: Employee equity grants at hire; refresh grants evaluated annually for high performers and critical hires.
- Competitive salary benchmarking completed annually by People-ops.

Time off and leave:
- Vacation: Flexible/unlimited paid time off; teams maintain coverage norms (minimum of 15 business days expected for full-time usage guidance).
- Parental leave: Primary caregiver up to 16 weeks fully paid; secondary caregiver up to 8 weeks.
- Sick leave, bereavement, and jury duty per regional law and People-ops policy.

Other perks:
- Stipends: Home office set-up stipend at hire ($500) and additional one-time ergonomic stipend where requested.
- Commuter benefit allowance in eligible regions.
- Company retreats: Annual all-hands; travel covered by Redwood.

Enrollment & questions: Benefits open enrollment windows and plan details are on the People-ops benefits portal. For policy exceptions, submit a ticket to people-ops@redwood.ai.

4) Hiring & Interviewing (overview for managers and hiring panels)

Hiring principles: Hire for mission alignment, technical competence, and growth mindset. We use structured interviews and scorecards to reduce bias. People-ops and recruiting own job postings, compensation bands, and offer approvals.

Typical interview loop (example for engineering):
1. Recruiter screen (30 min): role fit, compensation expectations, timeline.
2. Technical screen (45-60 min): coding/design problem or take-home (depending on level).
3. Onsite / virtual loop (3-4 interviews): system design, coding, behavioral/team fit, and manager interview.
4. Bar raiser or cross-team peer interview (for senior hires).
5. Offer & negotiation: recruiting sends formal offer; aim to close within 5 business days of final decision.

Interview logistics & scorecards:
- Use the standard scorecard template (link in the Manager toolkit). Each interviewer must provide written notes within 48 hours.
- Structured rubrics by level: technical depth, scope of impact, collaboration, and ownership.
- Candidate experience: recruiters own scheduling and candidate communication. Offer timelines and follow-ups are tracked in the ATS.

Diversity & inclusion: All roles require diverse slates when feasible. Hiring managers should partner with recruiting to ensure candidate sourcing aligns with our inclusion goals.

5) New Hire Onboarding Checklist (first 90 days)

Day 0-7 (preboarding and first week):
- Complete HR paperwork and benefits enrollment.
- IT access: request accounts via Okta; enable MFA and set up password manager.
- Equipment: confirm laptop and peripherals.
- Buddy assigned by team; first 1:1 schedule with manager.
- Orientation: company all-hands, product overview, security training.

Weeks 2-4:
- Team deep-dive: architecture overview, codebase walkthroughs, backlog orientation.
- Small starter task: close a small issue or add tests to learn the codebase.
- SLA & SLO training if joining platform/infra teams.

Months 1-3:
- Deliver first project milestone.
- Career conversation: 30/60/90 day check-ins documented in Performance tool.
- Feedback: New hire survey at 30 and 90 days; manager reviews results and follows up.

6) Internal Tools & Access

Primary tools (company-wide):
- Communication: Slack (main workspace with team channels and #all-hands).
- Documentation: Confluence (this space) for policies, runbooks, and playbooks.
- Source control: GitHub (organization: redwood-inference).
- Issue tracking: Linear for most teams; Product uses Jira where needed (team-specific).
- CI/CD: Buildkite pipelines; deployments coordinated via the infra dashboard.
- Identity & Access: Okta for SSO; groups managed via IT/People-ops.
- Secrets & keys: Vault (internal), and recommended use of LastPass/1Password for personal credentials.
- Analytics & monitoring: Datadog for logs/metrics; internal dashboards in Grafana.
- Payroll & expense: Gusto for payroll; Expensify for reimbursements.

Access process and approvals:
1. New hire automatic baseline access: Google Workspace, Slack, Confluence, Email, and People-ops portal.
2. Role-based access: Manager submits access request in the IT ticketing system for GitHub teams, Linear projects, Buildkite, and Datadog.
3. Sensitive access (prod infra, KMS, HSM): requires manager + infra owner approval and completion of security training whiteboard.

Security & MFA: All employees must enable MFA via Okta and complete annual security training. Privileged access reviews occur quarterly.

7) Manager responsibilities (summary)

- Recruiting & hiring: define role, write offer language, participate in interviews.
- Onboarding: schedule orientation, assign buddy, set first-quarter goals.
- Performance: conduct regular 1:1s, run calibration, document feedback.
- Development: own career conversations and recommend learning resources.

8) FAQ (short)

Q: How do I request a laptop upgrade?
A: Submit an IT request with manager approval; hardware replacements follow the 18-month refresh policy.

Q: Who approves equity refreshes?
A: People-ops in partnership with the employee's manager and the compensation committee.

Q: How long until I get GitHub access?
A: Role-based GitHub access is typically granted within 2 business days after manager request. Sensitive repos may require additional approvals.

9) Ownership, escalation, and contact points

- Document owner: People-ops (people-ops@redwood.ai).
- Hiring & Recruiting: recruiting@redwood.ai.
- IT & Access requests: it-support@redwood.ai (ticket required for role-based access).
- Benefits questions: benefits@redwood.ai.
